Resolves #21173

A redeploy that keeps its version now reaches returning visitors as one build. Every successful build publishes an identity. Each service worker registration keeps its own caches. A page of a new build starts its own workers and switches once.

- **A successful build stamps its id.** `buildScripts/util/buildId.mjs#stampBuildId()` runs after every successful build: `build-all`, `build-threads` (a single thread with `-t` included) and the ESM build. It writes the run's id into every app's `neo-config.json` and into the dist's service worker script. A failed build exits before the stamp, so it never publishes an id. `build-all` resolves one id and shares it with its steps through `process.env.NEO_BUILD_ID`.
- **The worker's identity is in its bytes.** `Neo.worker.ServiceBase` reads its `buildId` from the stamp, so the script changes with every build. A registration of the bare worker URL, from a client older than this change, also installs the new worker.
- **A cache belongs to its registration.** The name is `neo-runtime:<scope path>:<version>[:<buildId>]`. Activation deletes only that registration's superseded caches. The offline fallback reads only its own cache. The version-only caches of earlier workers stay: a sibling that is not updated yet may still serve them offline, and no scoped worker reads them.
- **The page moves to the new build once it can.** `Neo.main.addon.ServiceWorker` registers `…?buildId=<id>`, which installs a new build's worker even outside the worker's scope, where no navigation checks for updates.
  - A page that started on another build's worker asks the new one to activate, through `onSkipWaiting()`, once a second for up to a minute. Chromium can leave it waiting despite its install-time `skipWaiting()`.
  - The page reloads once the new worker is active, at most once per build in a tab's session.
  - Inside the scope the previous worker also controls the page and can keep the new one waiting until the page navigates. The page does not force that navigation (see Deltas).
- **A new build starts its own workers.** `Neo.worker.Manager#createWorker()` adds `?buildId=` to the worker URLs. A shared worker is keyed by URL and name, so a tab of the new build does not join the workers an older tab still runs. The names stay, since the Canvas worker reads its group from its name.

Evidence: L3 (Chromium receipts for the four controls of @neo-gpt-emmy's review and for redeploys inside and outside the scope) → L3 required (AC-4 asks for a replay receipt). No residuals.

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|

| AC-2 the newer build's worker deletes the older build's cache on activation; a unit test with two build identities | CI-covered: "activation under /dist/production/ …" and "… under /dist/esm/ deletes its own superseded caches, and keeps its sibling's and the version-only ones" (both transitions). "offline, a network-first request answers from its own registration's cache only" covers the fallback. |
| AC-3 development mode works as today | CI-covered: an unstamped worker has no build and keeps a version-only name within its scope. Without `Neo.config.buildId` the addon and the Manager use the URLs they used before. |
| AC-4 a replay receipt | Manual, not CI: see Test Evidence. |

## Deltas from ticket

- **The carriers**, the ticket's open choice: `neo-config.json` for the page (network-first, as @neo-opus-vega asked), and the stamp in the worker script for the worker. The stamp also catches builds that never run the App worker's config, e.g. `build-threads -t canvas`.
- **The build check lives in the addon, not the version handshake.** `Manager#checkServiceWorkerVersion()` runs only for a page the worker controls, and neomjs.com's root page is outside the worker's scope `/dist/production/`. The addon registers in both layouts. `Manager#reloadOnce()` is the reload throttle, moved out of the handshake so both reloads share it.
- **Cache names carry the scope.** Without it, two registrations of one origin (`/dist/production/`, `/dist/esm/`) deleted each other's caches (@neo-gpt-emmy's RA-1).
- **Worker URLs carry the build.** An older tab's shared workers otherwise served the new tab (RA-3).
- **The activation request.** The worker's install-time `skipWaiting()` alone often left it waiting in the replays. The page asks again, once a second for up to a minute, through the existing `onSkipWaiting()`.
- **No forced navigation inside the scope.** I tried a reload as soon as the new worker was installed: Chromium activates a waiting worker for a navigation. When that reload started while the previous worker was still serving the page's startup, it froze the page in 2 of 9 replays (no answer to `1+1` or to a screenshot). Inside the scope the switch therefore comes with the page's next navigation.
- **A run publishes its id after its last step.** `buildThreads.mjs` (once every selected environment built) and `esmodules.mjs` stamp when they run on their own; `all.mjs` runs both with `--no-stamp` (`BuildId.stampDeferred()`) and stamps development, production and `dist/esm` after its last step, so a later step that fails publishes nothing (RA-4, Round 2).

## Test Evidence

- **Unit:** `ServiceBase.spec.mjs`, `buildId.spec.mjs`, `esmDistTransforms.spec.mjs` and `buildDependencyResolution.spec.mjs` (which now copies `util/buildId.mjs` beside `buildThreads.mjs`), plus `test/playwright/unit/worker` and `test/playwright/unit/main`: green. The new `ServiceBase` arms fail against `dev`.
- **Publication** (RA-4, Round 2): `buildId.spec.mjs` runs the real `all.mjs` and `buildThreads.mjs` with `child_process` stubbed (`fixtures/childProcessStub.mjs`). An ESM or SEO step that fails leaves all three dist folders at their previous id, and an ESM-only run publishes only `dist/esm`; at `df3db5fe` an ESM failure published development and production, at `96bebc005f` the ESM step was not deferred, and at `0e6f196d42` a production thread that failed after development built left development published.
- **Receipts.** Headless Chromium against production builds of this branch, A and B, where B renames a Portal home heading to carry `(build B)`. A static server sends `no-store`, so only the worker can serve a previous build. A copy of the pages repo's root `index.html` puts the page outside the worker's scope, as on neomjs.com; the in-scope runs open `dist/production/apps/portal/index.html`.
  - **Redeploy:** a profile warmed twice on A, then B deployed. Outside the scope, B's heading shows on load 1 or 2 (3 runs). Inside the scope it shows on load 2 (3 runs): the controller moves from `…?buildId=buildA` to `…?buildId=buildB`, and only B's cache `neo-runtime:/dist/production/:13.4.0:buildB` remains.
  - **A warmed pre-feature client** (RA-2): a profile warmed twice on `dev`'s build (cache `neo-runtime-13.4.0`, bare worker URL), then B deployed. It shows B by its second load at the latest, with and without a browser restart in between (on the first load in the final runs). Its old cache stays, unread. A fresh profile shows B on its first load.
  - **Two tabs** (RA-3): tab 1 stays open on A, and a new tab 2 opens after B is deployed. Tab 2 renders B's heading and tab 1 still renders A's. The browser runs `appworker.js`, `canvasworker.js`, `dataworker.js` and `vdomworker.js` once with `?buildId=buildA` and once with `?buildId=buildB`.
  - **A Canvas-only rebuild** (RA-4): `build-threads -n -e prod -t canvas` on top of A, with a changed Canvas worker, as build C. `canvasworker.js` changes and `appworker.js` does not; the worker stamp and the Portal config both carry `buildC`. A page warmed on A, then reloaded once inside the scope, is controlled by `…?buildId=buildC` six seconds later and holds only C's cache. Both the bare `canvasworker.js` and the running `canvasworker.js?buildId=buildC` answer with C's bytes.
- **Controls on `dev`:**
  - **A same-version redeploy** keeps answering with A's chunks, inside and outside the scope.
  - **A release upgrade** (13.4.0 → 13.4.1) switches inside the scope through the version handshake's reload. Outside the scope it never switches cleanly within 90 seconds: the page runs the new main thread with A's cached chunk. This PR's registration URL covers that layout.

It stamps the run's id into every app's `neo-config.json` and into the dist's worker script. `ServiceBase` reads the id from that stamp; the registration's `?buildId=` stays only as the update trigger for a page outside the scope.
   - A legacy bare-URL registration's soft update therefore installs a worker with a new cache name, and its next navigation in scope activates it.
   - A failed build stamps nothing.
2. **A cache belongs to its registration (RA-1).** The name gains the registration scope, `neo-runtime-<scope>-<version>[-<build>]`.
   - Cleanup deletes only that scope's superseded caches.
   - Lookups use the worker's own cache instead of the origin-wide `caches.match()` in the network-first fallback.
   - Version-only legacy caches stay: a pre-feature sibling may still serve them offline, and no scoped worker reads them.
3. **Shared workers per build (RA-3).** `Manager#createWorker()` adds `?buildId=` to the worker script URL, so a tab of the new build starts its own App/VDom/Data/Canvas workers instead of joining an older tab's. Names stay as they are, since the Canvas worker parses its group from its name.

The four controls become the receipts: two registrations, a warmed legacy in-scope profile across a browser restart, two tabs with the old one kept open, and a Canvas-only rebuild.
